title: Business MRI™
tagline: A full-body scan of your business: operations, sales, marketing, automation, AI readiness and more.
description: 24 quick questions that scan every part of your business — operations, sales, marketing, customer experience, automation, AI readiness, leadership and systems — then show you exactly where you're losing time and money.

categories.label: Operations
categories.recommendation: Document your 3 most repeated processes as simple checklists, then automate or delegate the most time-consuming one this month.

categories.label: Sales
categories.recommendation: Set up a simple sales pipeline (even a spreadsheet works) and add automated follow-up so no lead is ever forgotten.

categories.label: Marketing
categories.recommendation: Pick ONE marketing channel that already brings you clients and double down on it with a consistent weekly rhythm before adding anything new.

categories.label: Customer Experience
categories.recommendation: Create an automated onboarding sequence and a review-request system — happy clients should be asked for a review within 48 hours.

categories.label: Automation
categories.recommendation: List every task you do more than 3 times a week. Automate the top 2 with simple tools like Zapier, Make or your CRM's built-in automations.

categories.label: AI Readiness
categories.recommendation: Start using AI for one real task this week — drafting emails, proposals or content. Small daily use builds the muscle fast.

categories.label: Leadership
categories.recommendation: Block 2 hours a week for working ON the business (strategy, systems, growth) and protect that time like a client meeting.

categories.label: Systems
categories.recommendation: Create one central place (a simple shared drive or Notion page) where every process, password and template lives — so the business runs on systems, not memory.

questions.text: How are your day-to-day processes documented?

options.label: They're not — everything lives in people's heads
A few notes here and there
Clear, up-to-date checklists for almost everything

questions.text: How often do tasks fall through the cracks or get done twice?

options.label: All the time — it's chaos some weeks
Almost never — we have a reliable system

questions.text: How much of your week goes to repetitive admin work (data entry, scheduling, copying info between tools)?

options.label: Under 2 hours — most of it is automated

questions.text: What happens when a new lead contacts your business?

options.label: We reply when we get a chance — sometimes days later
We usually reply within a day
We reply within a few hours
They get an instant automated response plus fast personal follow-up

questions.text: Do you know exactly how many leads you got last month and where they came from?

options.label: Yes — tracked precisely in a CRM

questions.text: How do you follow up with leads who don't buy right away?

options.label: We don't — if they go quiet, they're gone
We follow up once or twice manually
We have a loose follow-up routine
Automated follow-up sequence until they buy or opt out

questions.text: How consistent is your marketing?

options.label: We market only when things get slow
Sporadic — bursts of activity, then silence
Consistent weekly output on channels that work

questions.text: Do you have an email list you contact regularly?

options.label: A list, but we rarely email it
We email weekly or bi-weekly with valuable content

questions.text: Do you know your cost to acquire a new customer?

options.label: Yes, for every channel — we track it monthly

questions.text: What does a new client's first week with you look like?

options.label: It varies — we wing it every time
A polished, mostly automated onboarding experience

questions.text: How do you collect reviews and testimonials?

options.label: We don't ask — reviews happen by luck
We ask occasionally when we remember
We ask every happy client manually
Automated review requests after every job or milestone

questions.text: How quickly do existing clients get answers to their questions?

options.label: Fast replies plus self-serve answers (FAQ, portal, chatbot)

questions.text: How many of your repetitive tasks are automated today?

options.label: Most repetitive work runs without us touching it

questions.text: Do your main tools (calendar, CRM, invoicing, email) talk to each other?

options.label: No — we copy information between them by hand

questions.text: How are appointments booked with you?

options.label: Mostly manual with some online booking
Online booking with automated reminders and follow-ups

questions.text: How is your business using AI right now?

options.label: Occasional ChatGPT use by one person
Regular AI use for writing, research or admin
AI is built into our daily workflows

questions.text: How does your team feel about adopting AI tools?

options.label: Enthusiastic — we actively look for AI wins

questions.text: Is your business data (clients, projects, documents) organized enough for AI tools to use?
How much of your week is spent working ON the business (strategy, systems) vs IN it (delivery, firefighting)?

options.label: Zero — I'm buried in daily work
Significant, scheduled strategic time every week

questions.text: Do you have clear goals and numbers you review every month?

options.label: Goals exist but we rarely check them
Clear goals, weekly scorecard, monthly review rhythm

questions.text: If you took two weeks off, what would happen?

options.label: Things would grind to a halt
Business as usual — it runs without me

questions.text: Where does important business knowledge live (processes, templates, passwords)?

options.label: Scattered across email, notes and chat

questions.text: How does a new hire learn how you do things?

options.label: They shadow someone and figure it out
A structured onboarding with documented processes

questions.text: How standardized is the work you deliver to clients?

options.label: Every job is reinvented from scratch
Templates and checklists for core work

bands.label: Critical — Your business is running you
bands.summary: Your business depends heavily on manual effort and memory. That means long hours, missed leads and money left on the table every single week. The good news: businesses at this stage see the fastest, most dramatic wins from basic systems and automation.
actionPlan: Week 1: Write down every repetitive task you and your team do. Circle the 3 that eat the most time.
Week 1: Set up instant lead response — an auto-reply plus a same-hour follow-up rule for every new inquiry.
Week 2: Add online booking (e.g. Calendly) so appointments stop requiring back-and-forth emails.
Week 2: Put every lead into one list or simple CRM — nothing lives in inboxes anymore.
Week 3: Automate your #1 most repetitive task using your CRM, Zapier or an AI assistant.
Week 3: Create an automated review-request message that goes out after every completed job.
Week 4: Document your single most important process as a one-page checklist.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to map which fixes will pay off fastest for your specific business.

bands.label: At Risk — Working hard, leaking value
bands.summary: You have some structure, but too much still depends on manual effort. Leads slip away, hours vanish into admin work, and growth feels like it always requires more of YOU. Targeted automation could change that within 30 days.
actionPlan: Week 1: Audit where your hours went last week — mark every task that a tool or template could do.
Week 1: Tighten lead response to under 15 minutes with an auto-reply plus notification system.
Week 2: Build one automated follow-up sequence for leads that don't buy immediately.
Week 2: Connect your two most-used tools so data stops being copied by hand.
Week 3: Standardize client onboarding into a repeatable, mostly automated sequence.
Week 3: Start using AI weekly for drafting emails, proposals and content.
Week 4: Document your top 3 processes and assign clear owners.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to prioritize your next automations by ROI.

bands.label: Solid — Strong foundation, untapped upside
bands.summary: Your business runs well — better than most. But 'well' still hides real money: partially automated follow-up, inconsistent systems and underused AI are quietly capping your growth. You're in the perfect position to compound small optimizations into a big edge.
actionPlan: Week 1: Review your category scores below — pick your single weakest area as this month's focus.
Week 1: Set a measurable 30-day target for that area (e.g. 'respond to 100% of leads in 5 minutes').
Week 2: Automate the biggest remaining manual workflow end-to-end.
Week 2: Introduce AI into one client-facing process (proposals, reports or communication).
Week 3: Build a simple weekly scorecard with your 5 most important numbers.
Week 3: Train the team on the new systems so improvements stick.
Week 4: Delegate or automate one task that still needs the owner personally.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to identify advanced automations your competitors aren't using yet.

bands.label: Optimized — Now build your unfair advantage
bands.summary: Impressive. Your business runs on systems, not heroics. Your next opportunity isn't fixing leaks — it's using AI to widen the gap: faster delivery, smarter marketing and scale without headcount.
actionPlan: Week 1: Identify your most profitable service and map how AI could deliver it faster or better.
Week 1: Audit your tech stack for overlapping tools you can consolidate.
Week 2: Pilot an AI assistant for one internal function (research, reporting or client comms).
Week 2: Turn your best-performing marketing asset into an automated evergreen funnel.
Week 3: Build a knowledge base so AI tools can answer questions from YOUR business data.
Week 3: Set up quarterly systems reviews so nothing quietly decays.
Week 4: Explore a productized or scalable offer that runs mostly on systems.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to pressure-test your stack against what's now possible.
